body:
Tracking finding from the review of CultureMech PR #216 (which lands the #242 verdict in the hub).

When MIM bumps `scripts/.vendored_canon_ref` to pick up the three new hydration verdicts, records that the plausibility gate previously reported as `OK_ID_ONLY` — a hydrate label grounded to its anhydrous parent — will instead surface as one of `HYDRATE_ON_ANHYDROUS_TERM` / `ANHYDROUS_ON_HYDRATE_TERM` / `HYDRATION_STATE_MISMATCH`.

**Not a blocker:** all three are in `_WARN_VERDICTS`, not `_ERROR_VERDICTS`, so `just validate-products` enforce stays green. But:

- The correspondence **summary** and the label-drift **report** will gain new warning rows.
- Any curator waivers needed can go on the target `exceptions` allow-list (the three verdicts are wired into it).

Action for the sync PR: run `just validate-products` after the ref bump, eyeball the new warning population against `just report-hydrate-grounding` (the MIM-side measure from #240), and note the delta in the PR body so the count change is expected, not alarming.

comments.body:
Resolved by measurement in PR #262: the sync produced **zero** new warning rows, so there is no count delta for a sync PR to explain.

The reason is not clean data — the plausibility gate is checking `ontology_label` (the OBO canonical label), so every row short-circuits before the formula check. That is now tracked properly in #261, which supersedes this issue.

title: Sync note: hydration verdicts reclassify OK_ID_ONLY hydrate-on-anhydrous rows to warnings
